cost: O(total encoded bytes) streaming write time with buffered memory plus value formatting; read materializes O(file bytes + cells). Error preview takes at most 80 chars but row validation scans entire offending string.
description: Raw TSV representation and partial writes
forward: create truncates/creates file and writes joined header. row checks arity then writes columns left-to-right with tabs; Null emits backslash-N, strings reject tab/LF/CR/sentinel, integers decimal and booleans lowercase. Successful newline increments rows. finish flushes and returns count. read splits every file line without removing header, mapping exact sentinel to None; s/int check presence then parse.
inverse: Wrong arity cannot write any row prefix; invalid later cell cannot produce a successful row count increment. A literal backslash-N string cannot be represented as a successful non-NULL cell.

Given valid headerless encoded rows, None uniquely indicates Null and other cells are string observations. Value variants remain ambiguous: integer 1 and string 1 encode identically, true and boolean true likewise. Source lexical numeric spelling is not reconstructed by int.
read(backslash-N)=None and read(empty cell)=Some(empty). No quote or escape processing exists. JSON control escapes are ordinary bytes if already serialized before row.

Width check precedes all writes; separator precedes validation of each later string. After writing prefix then rejecting sentinel, observed file may end in prefix-tab and rows remains zero. Direct synthetic file test checks this exact effect.
I uses full signed-i64 decimal; int accepts parseable signed-i64 strings and rejects overflow/missing/null. Finite boundaries include MIN, MAX and MAX+1 string.
Tsv::create always writes a header line even for zero columns; read does not skip it. Writer/read are not direct inverse APIs unless caller separates headers.
limitations: Finite helper/fixture evidence only; no DuckDB integration or SQL semantics
Partial syntax projection; no macro expansion or full semantic proof
No executable approximate profile or speedup claim
state: rows counts only fully successful row calls, not physically complete lines after an earlier partial failure. Strings and NULL have disjoint encodings on the admitted domain; empty string remains Some(empty). Failure after earlier cells may leave a prefix in buffer/file.
